images.title: An *AI Customer Support* employee owns the ticket
images.sub: What it looks up, what it fixes within limits, what it hands to a person, and what the job costs.

images.name: vs-chatbot
images.title: Support chatbot vs. *AI Customer Support employee*
head: Support chatbot
AI Customer Support employee
rows: No, answers anyone the same way
Sees their orders, account and past tickets
Refunds, reships and changes within written limits
Hands the ticket to a person with a summary
Follows up until the ticket is closed
A named person on the team, with a full log
images.source: How the two usually compare. Products vary.

images.name: duties
images.title: The support job, *duty by duty*
rows: Answers email, chat, social messages and forms within minutes, at any hour, with the customer's details in front of it.
Order status, renewals, payments and appointments, checked in the systems the business runs on.
Address changes, resent invoices, small refunds, replacements and rebookings within written limits.
Hands exceptions to a person with the history, what was tried and a suggested reply.
Chases the supplier, technician or manager and writes back to the customer until it's closed.
A Friday report of ticket volume by reason and anything that looks like a product problem.

images.name: day-on-shift
images.title: A day at an *online kitchenware store*
rows: Answers 38 overnight messages. Most are order status, each with the tracking link.
A parcel the carrier left at the wrong address. It sends a replacement, inside the limit.
A customer disputes a charge with their bank. It pulls the order and hands it to the lead.
Changes a delivery address on an order that hasn't shipped yet.
A $420 refund request on a damaged set, above the limit. Drafted and held.
A customer says a pan handle broke and burned them. Sent straight to the lead, untouched.
Supplier confirms restock date. It writes to the 12 customers waiting on back orders.

images.name: setup
images.title: Setting up an *AI Customer Support employee*
steps: Sort the tickets you already have
Export a few hundred recent tickets and group them by reason. That list is the job.
Return policy, refund ceiling, who gets extra care, and what always goes to a person.
Helpdesk, store or billing, calendar and carrier tracking, with only the access the job needs.
It writes every reply and a person sends it. Each edit teaches it tone and policy.
Hand over one category at a time
Order status first, then changes, then refunds within the limit.
Someone reads the log and updates the rules when policies, products or carriers change.
